# FAQ-021 Engineering FAQ #21
Revision: Rev A

Q: What is the recommended spindle warm-up time before cutting on Machining CNC turning center #3 (EQ-P1-L3-CN03)?
A: Background: Proper spindle warm-up stabilizes bearing clearances and thermal gradients to ensure dimensional accuracy and tool life. For EQ-P1-L3-CN03, the specified spindle warm-up time is 27 minutes. Rationale: Allowing the spindle to reach thermal equilibrium reduces runout drift and avoids premature reloads. Example: Start the spindle at idle RPM and monitor for consistent runout readings before initiating a finishing pass. Records to keep: Log the start and ready timestamps for each shift run in the machine's downtime log and note any deviations in the spindle warm-up period in the corrective action record. See SOP-P1-L3-04 for machine-specific pre-start checks.

Q: How often should the main roll bearings be lubricated on Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P1-L1-RR01)?
A: Background: Proper lubrication of main roll bearings is critical to prevent metal-to-metal contact, overheating, and surface defects on rolled parts. Interval: The main roll bearing lubrication interval for EQ-P1-L1-RR01 is 120 hours. Rationale: A timed lubrication schedule ensures replenishment of lubricant film before degradation, based on operating duty and bearing design. Example: If the mill accumulates extended runtime during production runs, schedule lubrication actions according to the recorded run-hours clock and before any planned heavy roll changeover. Records to keep: Maintain the bearing lubrication log showing timestamped lubrication events, lubricant type used, and the technician initials. Reference SOP-P1-L1-02 for approved grease types and lubrication procedure steps.

Q: What warm-up procedure is used for the spindle on the Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02)?
A: Background: Each CNC turning center may have different spindle-bearing preheat characteristics depending on bearing preload and environmental conditions. The spindle warm-up time for EQ-P1-L1-CN02 is 21 minutes. Rationale: Following the prescribed warm-up ensures concentricity and prevents thermal shocks when transitioning to cut speeds. Example: Apply the spindle warm-up cycle in the machine control panel, observe vibration meters, and confirm that tool offsets remain within established control limits before cutting. Records to keep: Document the warm-up run in the machine run log, including operator name, start and end times, and any anomalies found. SOP-P1-L3-04 contains control panel warm-up sequences and verification points.

Q: What alarm setpoint should maintenance verify on the dust collection system for the Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03)?
A: Background: Dust collector differential pressure monitors protect process quality and equipment by indicating when filter media is loaded or when airflow is restricted. Alarm setpoint: The dust collector pressure drop alarm for EQ-P3-L4-SB03 is 1510 Pa. Rationale: Setting and verifying the alarm at the specified differential pressure ensures filtration efficiency and prevents particulate bypass into the cabinet or downstream processes. Example: During filter replacement, reset the differential sensor after confirming the pressure drop falls below the alarm threshold and record the reset action. Records to keep: Keep a filter maintenance log with pressure readings before and after service, alarm event entries including trigger timestamp, and actions taken. See SOP-P3-L4-02 for filter change and sensor calibration procedures.

Q: What minimum coil cooling water flow is required to safely operate Hot Forge induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P2-L1-IH02)?
A: Background: Induction heaters rely on adequate water flow to cool coils and power electronics; insufficient flow risks coil damage and compromised heating profiles. Minimum flow: The coil cooling water flow minimum for EQ-P2-L1-IH02 is 55 L/min. Rationale: Maintaining flow at or above the stated minimum sustains heat removal capacity and avoids thermal runaway in coil windings. Example: Verify flow using the installed flowmeter prior to each production run; if flow readout is below the minimum, lock out the heater and follow the pump and piping troubleshooting checklist. Records to keep: Log flowmeter readings at startup and after any maintenance, record pump service events, and include any flow-related incidents in the equipment failure report. Consult SOP-P1-L1-02 for water quality and pump maintenance guidance.

Related documents: SOP-P1-L1-02, SOP-P1-L3-04, SOP-P3-L4-02

Document control note: Retain warm-up, lubrication, alarm, and flow logs with the equipment history record for each listed asset (EQ-P1-L3-CN03, EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02, EQ-P3-L4-SB03, EQ-P2-L1-IH02) and reference this FAQ when performing audits or training.
